subject: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding — regional capacity decision & acceptance criteria
messages:

Subject: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding — regional capacity decision & acceptance criteria

Hi Alex / Samantha,

Thanks again for choosing Redwood Dedicated. This thread is to capture the kick-off items for the GPU pool provisioning, autoscaling/burst policy, and our regional selection recommendation so we can lock the acceptance criteria and next steps.

TL;DR — proposed path: provision a US-central pool (primary), reserve cross-region burst capacity in US-west, enable autoscale with a 15% prewarm buffer for daytime traffic, and run a week-long activation validation using your inference workload set.

Key asks for Orion prior to provisioning:
- Confirm the 99/95 p99 latency SLOs you want pinned to this pool (we have defaults but want your confirmation).
- Share expected QPS distribution by hour (sample CSV attached) and top-3 model variants we’ll serve.
- Confirm greenlight on us-west as burst region (if you'd prefer eu-west instead, flag it).

I attached an implementation checklist and our capacity-estimates spreadsheet to illustrate assumptions. Proposed acceptance criteria (high level):
1) All prewarm and baseline capacity meets >95% of sampled traffic within 200ms of target SLO during validation window.
2) Failover routing to burst region completes within configured fallback window (2 min) without request loss.
3) Autoscaling policy sustains steady-state and handles 3x peak synthetic load for 10 minutes without errors.

We’ll schedule a 30-minute sync Friday to finalize decisions if that works for your team.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

+1 415-555-0129

Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding — regional capacity decision & acceptance criteria

Kimberly —

Appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers:
- SLOs: we'll target p95=1200ms, p99=1800ms for the first phase while we optimize models; if we see headroom after validation we may tighten to p99=1500ms.
- QPS distribution: attached is a 7-day sample (hourly). Peak is PST afternoon for our east-coast customers.
- Models: core-guardian-v2, summarizer-lite-1, reranker-proto.
- Burst region: agree with US-west for reduced egress and latency to west coast customers; no EU capacity needed for Phase 1.

Friday 10:00am PT works for a sync. One ask — can Redwood provide a short-runbook we can hand to our SREs showing the autoscale thresholds and failover steps?

Thanks,
Alex

Subject: RE: Dedicated GPU pool onboarding — regional capacity decision & acceptance criteria

Team —

Adding technical notes ahead of the Friday sync to make sure we surface constraints:

1) Provisioning plan: We will spin a primary pool in us-central with the following initial config: 12 x A100-equivalent slots (baseline), 6 x A100-equivalent slots reserved for burst in us-west. Final numbers may change after we run the traffic projection in the CSV.

2) Autoscale policy (proposal):
- Target utilization: 60% (node-level GPU utilization), scale-up threshold 70% sustained for 90s, scale-down threshold 45% sustained for 120s.
- Prewarm buffer: 15% of baseline active nodes during business hours (08:00-18:00 local).
- Max burst factor: 3x baseline; burst budget will be metered and billed separately per SOW.

3) Routing/failover:
- Smart routing will prefer primary region; on 5xx rate >2% or average latency > p95 target for 2 minutes, traffic will redirect to us-west burst group with a graceful 30s ramp to preserve session affinity where possible.

4) Validation tasks for activation window:
- Run customer workload for 2x 1-hour windows: baseline and then 3x peak synthetic to validate autoscale and KV cache warmup.
- Run end-to-end request tracing to ensure KV cache hits are >75% after warmup.

I'll add these items to the doc in Drive and draft a 1-page SRE runbook for Alex's team. Rishi — please confirm whether the prewarm buffer should be hourly or per rolling 30-min window; that affects our bin-packing and cost estimate.

-Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Quick answers and acceptance checklist prior to provisioning:

- Prewarm cadence: use rolling 30-minute windows for prewarm evaluation. This gives faster reaction to diurnal spikes while keeping cost bounded.
- Capacity numbers: based on Orion's QPS sample, bump baseline to 16 x A100-equivalent slots and keep 6 x burst slots in us-west. I'll update the capacity estimates spreadsheet.
- Acceptance steps we will run after provisioning (must all pass):
  1) Latency validation: run customer traffic for 60 minutes and confirm p95/p99 thresholds (per Alex) are met.
  2) Autoscale exercise: induce a 3x synthetic spike for 10 minutes and verify no more than 1% 5xx during the event.
  3) Failover test: simulate primary region degradation and verify traffic shifts to burst region within 2 minutes with no data loss.
  4) Billing sanity: compare expected vs projected egress and burst meter billing estimates.

I will pick a provisioning window next week (Tuesday evening PT) and send calendar invites for the activation validation. Monica — please share the SRE runbook draft before Monday so we can give it to Orion.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
